title: Async compact race causing transient stale reads and memory spikes
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Brief: Following a capacity event on 2026-02-27 we observed repeated transient stale reads from the prefix/KV cache coincident with a sustained memory growth spike. Root cause investigation shows an asynchronous compaction/eviction interaction: compaction worker marked slab segments for reclamation while concurrent insert/lookup code was re-linking entries, leading to short-lived duplicate entries and KV reference-counting misalignment. The result was: transient stale read windows (0.5–2s) for some keys, and a ~18% aggregate heap increase which triggered autoscaler churn. This ticket tracks mitigation tasks, short-term safety fixes, and follow-ups.
impact_summary:
- Incident window: 2026-02-27 03:12 UTC to 2026-02-27 03:42 UTC
- Affected endpoints: generation-api and rerank service (traffic routed to fallback models during spikes)
- Observable effects: 95th–99th latency p99 spikes (+300ms), memory growth ~18% above baseline, 2 customer incidents reported (internal SRE alerts)
- Customer impact: degraded tail latency, one customer reported throttling; no data loss
timeline: 2026-02-27 03:12 UTC — Pager alert: autoscaler triggered; memory trending up on serving fleet for region us-west-2
2026-02-27 03:18 UTC — Engineering triage: noticed elevated KV cache slab usage and increased collisions in slab allocator metrics
2026-02-27 03:25 UTC — Mitigation: temporarily reduce prefix cache admission probability for long-prefix entries (runtime flag), which reduced OOM pressure
2026-02-27 03:30 UTC — Rollback: rolled back recent slab-compaction tuning commit (runtimerepo@a1b2c3) suspected in interplay
2026-02-27 03:42 UTC — Memory and latencies returned to baseline after mitigation; incident declared mitigated
2026-03-01 — Root cause analysis started; reproducer created in staging using synthetic long-tail sequence workload
2026-03-04 — Reproducer showed race between compaction finalizer and concurrent insert path that re-linked tombstoned entries
2026-03-08 — Initial patch submitted to fix refcounting and add compaction fencing (PR #1442)
2026-03-11 — Additional stress tests run; observed one remaining window under extreme contention; more robust fencing required
action_items: A1 — Hotfix: Add compaction-to-writer fencing to guarantee compaction sees a consistent view (owner: Liam Chen, due: 2026-03-15)
A2 — Safety guard: Add temporary backpressure that caps concurrent compaction jobs to 1 per node (owner: Priya Singh, due: 2026-03-13)
A3 — Telemetry: Emit compaction-start/finish + per-slab refcount drift metric; add alert if drift > 5% for 10m (owner: Sofia Patel, due: 2026-03-09)
A4 — Verifier: Add unit + randomized concurrency tests reproducer to CI (owner: Marco Ruiz, estimate: 2) due: 2026-03-18
A5 — Long-term: Evaluate adaptive eviction hysteresis and KV admission policy to avoid re-insert thrash under compaction (owner: EngArch, due: 2026-04-01)
A6 — Runbook: Update prefixcache runbook with steps for compaction-induced leaks and emergency mitigation flags (owner: Oncall SRE, due: 2026-03-14)
decisions: D1 — Immediate course: prioritize correctness (refcount/fencing) over performance micro-optimizations. Restore compaction tuning only after proof via stress tests.
D2 — Rolling upgrade: hotfix deployed as canary to 5% of nodes in us-west-2 before full rollout.
D3 — Observability: add compaction/fence metrics to Console per-node dashboard; include event annotations during future rollouts.
followups: F1 — Audit: Full code audit of slab allocator edge cases and reference counting across write/compact/delete paths (owner: Security & Reliability, due: 2026-04-05)
F2 — Performance: Re-run kernel selection benchmarks with fencing in place to quantify latency regression; target <2% p99 overhead (owner: Perf team, due: 2026-04-10)
F3 — Release notes: Document behavior change and emergency flags in runtime-1.20 release notes (owner: Docs, due: 2026-03-20)
